h1: Nursing staffing agencies: 10 firms sorted by how they actually fill shifts
seoTitle: Nursing Staffing Agencies: 10 Firms by Staffing Model (2026)
description: Ten nursing staffing agencies grouped by the job they do best: travel contracts, rapid response, per diem apps, franchise networks and international RN pipelines, with where each is based and what to check before you sign.
lead: A director of nursing with three open night shifts and a unit going on a 13 week census spike needs two different agencies, not one. This guide sorts nurse staffing firms by the model they run, so you call the right kind first.
shortAnswer: Short answer: for 13 week travel contracts at scale, start with Aya Healthcare. For a crisis opening or a labor action, Fastaff built the rapid response model. For per diem shifts in skilled nursing and post-acute settings, IntelyCare and Nursefinders are the first calls. If the gap is permanent and structural, the international pipelines at Avant and Conexus MedStaff take a year or more but end with your own employee.

choose.h: Name the model before the firm.
choose.p: Per diem fills a single shift, travel fills roughly a quarter, rapid response fills a gap that opens this week, and international recruitment fills a permanent seat on a long lead time. Most bad agency experiences come from buying one model to solve another.

choose.h: Ask for the certification letter.
choose.p: Several firms below hold The Joint Commission's Health Care Staffing Services certification. Ask for the current letter rather than relying on a logo on the website, and ask how credential files are shared with your compliance team.

choose.h: Get the bill rate structure in writing.
choose.p: Ask whether the quote is an all-in hourly bill rate or a pay rate plus markup, what overtime and holiday multipliers apply, and whether there is a conversion fee if you hire the nurse permanently.

choose.h: Check who your account actually sits with.
choose.p: Several of these firms are now one brand inside a larger group. Ask which entity signs the contract, who handles escalations, and whether a vendor management system or a managed services program sits between you and the agency.

firms.name: Aya Healthcare
firms.model: Travel nursing, per diem app, workforce software
firms.bestFor: Large travel contracts plus the software to manage them
firms.summary: Aya describes itself as America's largest travel nursing and allied health staffing agency. Alongside travel contracts it sells workforce software to hospitals: the LotusOne vendor management system, a Workforce AI demand matching tool, an app-based Shifts product for per diem and float pool work, and CoreHire for permanent hiring.
good: You need many travel nurses across several units or sites
You want agency supply and a VMS from one vendor
watch: If Aya also runs your VMS, ask how other agencies are treated in the order queue
Large accounts get the most attention; small single unit orders may not

firms.name: Fastaff
firms.model: Rapid response travel nursing
firms.bestFor: Urgent openings that cannot wait for a normal travel start date
firms.summary: Fastaff was founded in 1989 and introduced what it calls the Rapid Response model: deploying experienced nurses quickly to hospitals facing urgent shortages, with guaranteed delivery and a focus on hard to fill specialties. It holds The Joint Commission's Gold Seal for staffing and is one of eight brands in the Ingenovis Health group, which also includes Trustaff, USN and VISTA Staffing.
good: A unit needs experienced nurses within days, not weeks
You want one group that can also cover longer travel and labor disruption needs
watch: Rapid response rates are a premium product; budget for it as an exception
Clarify which Ingenovis brand owns the order so escalations go to the right team

firms.name: IntelyCare
firms.model: App based per diem and part-time nursing
firms.bestFor: Skilled nursing and post-acute facilities filling shifts week to week
firms.summary: IntelyCare runs an app that matches nurses and nursing assistants to open shifts, and calls itself a healthcare talent platform rather than a traditional agency. In 2023 it moved to a regional structure and added full-time and part-time hiring alongside shifts. It holds The Joint Commission's Health Care Staffing Services certification.
good: Your gaps are individual shifts in long term care or post-acute settings
Schedulers want to post and fill shifts themselves
watch: Check coverage in your specific region before signing
An app fills shifts, it does not build unit continuity; pair it with a retention plan

firms.name: Nursefinders
firms.model: Per diem and local contract staffing
firms.bestFor: Local per diem coverage backed by a large parent
firms.summary: Nursefinders has placed nurses and allied professionals for more than 40 years and now focuses on per diem and local jobs in nursing, allied health and healthcare support. It is Joint Commission accredited and part of AMN Healthcare, which gives buyers a route into AMN's travel and workforce programs if needs grow.
good: You want local nurses who can pick up recurring shifts
You may later want travel or managed services from the same parent
watch: Local branch strength varies by metro; ask for fill rates in your market
Confirm whether orders route through an AMN program or directly

firms.name: Favorite Healthcare Staffing
firms.model: Per diem, local, travel and permanent placement
firms.bestFor: Facilities that want one vendor across every contract length
firms.summary: Favorite started placing travel nurses in 1991 and now offers per diem, local and travel assignments, temp to perm and direct hire, plus recruitment process outsourcing and a managed services program. It has held The Joint Commission certification since 2005 and says it has appeared on Staffing Industry Analysts' largest healthcare staffing firms list every year since 2009. It describes itself as part of a larger multinational group, with Espirita as its international sister company.
good: You want per diem and travel from one contract
You may outsource part of permanent nurse recruiting later
watch: Ask which parts of the group serve your account
Broad menus can mean thinner specialty depth; ask for references in your specialty

firms.name: ATC Healthcare
firms.model: Franchise network, per diem and contract
firms.bestFor: Local coverage from an owner operated office
firms.summary: ATC Healthcare has run a healthcare staffing franchise for close to 40 years, with locally owned offices across the United States. It serves hospitals, residential care programs, public health departments, school systems, medical groups and municipal governments.
good: You value a local owner you can call directly
Public sector and school nursing needs sit alongside hospital shifts
watch: Quality depends on the local franchise; meet the office that will serve you
Multi-state systems may deal with several franchise owners

firms.name: Gifted Healthcare
firms.model: Travel, local and per diem nursing
firms.bestFor: Gulf South facilities mixing contract lengths
firms.summary: Gifted Healthcare places nurses on travel assignments, local contracts and per diem shifts, and also covers allied health and education based roles such as school nursing and behavioral interventionists.
good: You need RNs, LPNs and CNAs across contract types
School and behavioral roles sit in the same budget as clinical nursing
watch: Confirm specialty depth for ICU, OR and L&D before relying on it
Ask for state by state fill history outside its home region

firms.name: Stability Healthcare
firms.model: Travel nursing and allied, permanent roles
firms.bestFor: Travel RN coverage from a smaller, clinician focused firm
firms.summary: Stability Healthcare places travel registered nurses and allied clinicians, lists permanent jobs alongside contracts, and runs a managed services offering for facilities. Its public job pages publish weekly pay ranges by state, which helps buyers sanity check the rates they are quoted.
good: You want a firm that publishes pay data openly
Med-surg, tele, ICU and ER travel needs
watch: Smaller bench than the national giants for very large orders
Ask how quickly it can credential for your state

firms.name: Avant Healthcare Professionals
firms.model: International nurse recruitment
firms.bestFor: Permanent RN seats filled from overseas
firms.summary: Avant has recruited internationally educated nurses for U.S. health systems for more than 20 years and is a member of the Jackson Healthcare family of companies. It holds The Joint Commission certification and stresses ethical recruitment practices that it says meet or exceed global standards.
good: Vacancies are structural and you can plan a year or more ahead
You want nurses who become long term members of your staff
watch: Immigration timelines are outside the agency's control
Read the commitment period and repayment terms that apply to nurses

firms.name: Conexus MedStaff
firms.model: International nurse recruitment
firms.bestFor: International pipelines with Philippines and UK teams
firms.summary: Conexus MedStaff was founded in Houston in 2011 and is led by CEO Andrew Moreton. It is family owned, with teams in the UK and the Philippines, and guides nurses through immigration, licensure and relocation into U.S. roles.
good: You want a second international pipeline alongside an incumbent
Relocation support matters for retention in your market
watch: Same lead time caveats as any international program
Ask how many nurses it currently has in the visa queue for your specialty

inhouse.h: When your own recruiting team should do it instead
p: Agency nurses solve a capacity problem, but every agency hour costs more than an employed hour, and none of it builds a bench. If the same units call an agency every quarter, the cheaper fix is usually a recruiting function that keeps a warm pipeline of local nurses: a CRM of past applicants and former staff, a scheduler that books interviews quickly, and outreach that reaches nurses on their phones.

Software can carry part of that load. Our high volume hiring stack covers the scheduling and screening side, and the sourcing tools category compares the search layer. Tools such as Noon's nurse sourcing workflow treat licensure as a hard filter and contact clinicians by email and SMS, which is how most nurses prefer to be reached between shifts.

sections.h: Reading an agency quote
p: Ask every firm on your shortlist to quote the same scenario: one night shift RN in your busiest unit for 13 weeks, and one per diem shift next Saturday. Comparing the two answers side by side shows you which firms are really travel shops and which are really local shops, regardless of what the website says.

Then ask what happens at week 14. A firm that only talks about extensions is selling continuity; a firm that offers a conversion path is selling you a hire. Both are fine, as long as you know which one you are buying. Our guide to applicant tracking systems covers how to keep agency and direct applicants in one record.

faq.q: What is the difference between a per diem and a travel nursing agency?
faq.a: A per diem agency fills individual shifts with nurses who live locally, often booked a few days ahead. A travel agency places a nurse on a fixed contract, commonly around 13 weeks, usually from outside your area.

faq.q: Do nursing staffing agencies need to be certified?
faq.a: Certification is voluntary, but many hospitals require it. The Joint Commission's Health Care Staffing Services certification is the most common; ask for the current letter during contracting.

faq.q: Can I hire an agency nurse permanently?
faq.a: Usually, but most contracts include a conversion fee or a minimum number of worked hours before conversion. Read that clause before the first shift, not after you want to make an offer.

faq.q: How do I list my staffing firm on this page?
faq.a: Use the listing details at the end of the guide. We review every request against the same criteria as the firms above.

description: Ten staffing agencies in Dallas with a verified office in the metro, from Noel Road and North Central Expressway to Plano, Irving and Garland, sorted by the kind of hire each handles best.
lead: Which Dallas staffing agency should you call? It depends less on the brand and more on the seat: a contract controller, a cybersecurity engineer and forty warehouse pickers are three different phone calls. Every firm below has a staffed office in the Dallas area, and we list the street so you know who is local.
shortAnswer: Short answer: for finance and office roles with a written guarantee, start with Frontline Source Group or Robert Half. For IT contractors at scale, TEKsystems and LaSalle Network. Clinical and revenue cycle roles go to Medix in Irving, and hourly warehouse or call center volume to Snelling. If you want a Texas owned firm, Choice Specialists is the Dallas arm of Burnett Specialists.

choose.h: Decide whether you are buying hours or a hire.
choose.p: Temporary and contract work is priced as an hourly bill rate; direct hire is priced as a fee on first year salary. Ask each firm to quote both for the same role, because the gap tells you how much the firm wants each kind of order.

choose.h: Ask which office will actually work the order.
choose.p: Several national firms serve Dallas from Plano or Irving. That is fine for remote friendly roles, but for on-site interviews or shift work you want the recruiter who knows the commute from Garland to the Stemmons corridor.

choose.h: Get the guarantee terms, not the slogan.
choose.p: Replacement guarantees range from a few weeks to multiple years. Read what triggers a refund or a free replacement, and whether layoffs or role changes void it.

choose.h: Check conversion fees before day one.
choose.p: If a temp might become permanent, ask how many worked hours remove the conversion fee. Texas employers often lose money here simply because nobody asked.

inhouse.h: When Dallas employers should recruit directly
p: The metroplex has one of the deepest professional labor pools in the country, which cuts both ways: candidates are plentiful, but so are competing offers. If you place the same accountant or developer profile through an agency every quarter, those fees would usually fund an internal recruiter within a year.

A lean internal setup needs three things: an applicant tracking system that keeps past applicants searchable, a scheduling tool that books interviews within a day, and a way to reach passive candidates. For active applicants, start with a shortlist of job posting sites rather than posting everywhere. Our staffing agency stack shows what agencies themselves run, and the applicant tracking systems category compares the record keeping layer.

sections.h: How Dallas pricing usually works
p: Ask every shortlisted firm the same two questions: what is the bill rate for a contract staff accountant for twelve weeks, and what is the placement fee for a permanent one at your salary band. Firms that answer quickly have the market data; firms that need a week are probably building a quote from scratch.

For light industrial and call center work, ask for the pay rate and the markup separately, and confirm who handles drug screening and background checks. Our background check category covers the vendors agencies typically use.

faq.q: Which staffing agency in Dallas is best for temporary office work?
faq.a: For clerical and administrative temps, Choice Specialists, Robert Half and Snelling all list administrative staffing from Dallas offices. Ask each for its fill time on a one week assignment.

faq.q: Do Plano and Irving offices count as Dallas agencies?
faq.a: For most hiring, yes. Plano and Irving are inside the Dallas metro, and several national firms run their North Texas teams from there.

faq.q: How much do Dallas staffing agencies charge?
faq.a: Contract roles are billed as an hourly rate that includes the worker's pay plus a markup; permanent placements are usually a percentage of first year salary. Rates vary by role, so request written quotes.

faq.q: Can my firm be added to this list?

faq.a: Choice Specialists lists payrolling services, which lets you put a worker you found yourself on the agency's payroll.

lead: How many staffing firms does a mid-sized employer actually need? Usually two or three, each matched to a different kind of hire. The ten firms below are all national, all still independent brands under the parents named here as of November 2026, and all verified on their own websites this week. They are grouped by what they are built to do, not by revenue, because a firm that fills forklift shifts by the morning is a poor choice for a controller search and the reverse is just as true.
shortAnswer: Short answer: for specialized contract and permanent hires in finance, technology, legal and administration, start with Robert Half. For IT contractors at volume, call Insight Global or Kforce. For locally owned offices in smaller markets, Express Employment Professionals. For same-day industrial and event labor, PeopleReady.

choose.h: Decide whether you are buying hours or a hire.
choose.p: Contract staffing bills an hourly markup for as long as the person works for you; direct hire charges a one-time fee, usually a share of first-year salary. Many firms on this list do both, but most have a center of gravity, and the recruiters you meet will be trained on that side of the business.

choose.h: Match the firm's specialty to the job family.
choose.p: A generalist branch can fill a receptionist role in a day, but a SOX auditor or a Kubernetes engineer needs a recruiter who works that niche every week. Ask how many people in that exact job family the local team placed in the last quarter.

choose.h: Ask who owns the candidate relationship.
choose.p: Franchised networks are run by local owners, so service quality varies by office. Company-owned branches follow one playbook. Neither is better, but you should know which you are signing with before you negotiate terms.

choose.h: Get the conversion terms in writing.
choose.p: If you may hire a contractor permanently, agree the conversion fee and the hours after which it drops before the first person starts. This is the clause most often disputed later.

Our applicant tracking systems category and the high volume hiring stack cover both, and the background check guide compares screening vendors.

inhouse.h: When a Phoenix employer should recruit directly

h1: Fashion recruitment agencies: 10 firms for design, product and brand hiring

lead: Pick the agency by the job, not by the brand names on its homepage. The ten below split into freelance and temp desks, contingency recruiters for corporate roles, and executive search firms. choose.h: Decide between freelance, contingency and retained.
choose.p: Freelance and temp work is billed hourly with the agency's margin built in. Contingency recruiters charge a share of first year salary only when you hire, while retained search firms take part of the fee up front. Pick the model before you call, because firms quote differently for each.

choose.h: Test category knowledge in the first call.

choose.h: Check where the candidates live.

inhouse.h: When a fashion brand should recruit in house
p: Brands that hire the same roles every season, such as associate designers, merchandising assistants or store managers, usually save money by building their own pipeline. sections.h: What to compare in fashion agency quotes

faq.q: How much do fashion recruiters charge?

faq.q: Can I hire freelance fashion designers through an agency?
faq.a: Yes. 24 Seven, SBH Fashion, Atrium and Emerging Blue all offer freelance or temporary fashion staffing, billed by the hour.

inhouse.h: When to recruit in house instead
p: Agencies earn their markup on spikes, hard to reach shifts and roles you fill once a year. If you hire the same front desk, cook or warehouse role every month, a careers page, a steady job board budget and a quick text based screening step often cost less than a permanent markup on every hour worked.

For salaried roles, compare the agency fee against the time a hiring manager or internal recruiter would need to source the role. A shortlist from a strong sourcing tool plus an applicant tracking system can cover recurring professional hiring without a placement fee.

If your site is in Henderson, Insight Global, PrideStaff and AtWork all name Henderson in their local coverage.

sections.h: Convention and event staffing is its own category
p: Trade shows need setup crews, registration staff, ushers and brand ambassadors for a few days at a time. General light industrial firms can supply labor, but an office with an event and convention desk, such as PrideStaff, is more likely to have people who already know badge pickup, venue check-in and load-in schedules. Book these orders weeks ahead of large shows, because every exhibitor is asking at the same time.

lead: Five of the nine firms on this list give a Poplar Avenue address for their Memphis office, while the two warehouse specialists sit on East Raines Road and Hacks Cross Road in the southeast of the city. That spread is the first thing to check when you pick an agency here, because the branch that takes your order is the branch that sends replacements. We read the Memphis location page of every firm below on November 12, 2026, and split them into warehouse and logistics specialists, general staffing offices and professional desks, with the address each one lists today.
shortAnswer: Short answer: for warehouse and distribution volume, call ProLogistix or Staffmark first. For mixed office and light industrial orders, compare PrideStaff and Randstad. For accountants and IT contractors, start with Vaco or Robert Half.

choose.h: Decide whether the role is hourly or salaried first.
choose.p: Memphis agencies divide sharply. Industrial firms bill by the hour and compete on fill speed and shift coverage; professional firms place accountants, analysts and engineers and compete on candidate quality. A firm that is strong at one is rarely the best call for the other.

choose.h: Map the branch to your dock door.
choose.p: A Raines Road or Hacks Cross Road branch is a short drive from the southeast distribution corridor, while the Poplar Avenue offices are closer to East Memphis offices and hospitals. Replacement workers come from the branch, so distance changes how fast a no show gets covered.

choose.h: Ask how peak season is staffed.
choose.p: Parcel and retail fulfillment work peaks around the winter holidays. Ask each firm how many extra workers it placed last peak, whether it runs onsite coordinators, and what happens when your order doubles in a week.

choose.h: Get the full cost in one line.
choose.p: Request the pay rate, bill rate, overtime multiplier and temp to hire conversion fee for the exact role. Comparing markups alone hides differences in overtime billing and conversion terms.

inhouse.h: When Memphis employers should recruit directly
p: Agency markups make sense for peak season, night shifts and roles you fill once. If you hire the same picker, packer or customer service role every month all year, the markup on every hour worked can cost more than a recruiter's salary. A careers page with a short mobile application, a standing job board budget and fast text screening usually fill steady hourly roles at a lower cost per hire.

Salaried roles follow the same logic. Before paying a permanent placement fee for a recurring role, see whether a sourcing tool and your applicant tracking system can produce the shortlist. Agencies that want to keep their own desks lean use the same tools; Noon's overview for staffing agency recruiters shows one way AI sourcing and email and SMS outreach fit into a desk.

sections.h: How the list splits by type
p: Two firms here do almost nothing but industrial work: ProLogistix and Staffmark. Four are generalists that mix office and plant roles: Randstad, PrideStaff, Manpower and Surge. Three are professional firms: Robert Half, Vaco and Insight Global. Most employers end up with one firm from the first or second group for hourly work and one from the third for salaried roles.

Randstad is the only firm here that publishes a separate branch for manufacturing and logistics, in Bartlett. Robert Half is the only one with a downtown office, which matters for firms near the riverfront and the medical district.

p: We started from firms with a published Memphis area address, opened each location page with a standard browser on November 12, 2026, and kept only firms whose page loaded and named a local office. One local agency was dropped because its domain now shows a for sale page. Addresses and specialties come from each firm's own page; we did not use review site ratings to order the list.
